scoreRule: 1 point per objective question or position and 1 point per teacher-reviewed written item; local grade proposal only
description: Independent teacher-supervised B2 listening assessment about Harrison Ford's reflections on his career, collaboration and responsibility. No student media player.

variant.goal: Interpret the speaker's message about professional identity, shared success and gratitude, and support brief explanations with details from the speech.

gist.title: Which statement best captures the lesson Ford draws from his career?
options: A career should be judged mainly by how many awards it brings.
Finding one's place and recognising others can matter as much as public success.
Early uncertainty is a sign that a person has chosen the wrong profession.
Film actors are more successful when they work independently.
gist.why: His reflections connect the discovery of a calling to gratitude for the people who helped him.

gist.title: What does the speaker's combination of humour and thanks achieve?
options: It makes his reflections personal without presenting success as a solitary achievement.
It suggests that the audience should not take the award seriously at all.
It shows he is uncertain whether he wants to continue working.
It moves attention away from the colleagues who supported him.
gist.why: Self-deprecating jokes sit alongside a sincere acknowledgement of collaboration.

detail.title: Why is the reference to his college experience significant?
options: It shows he had already achieved success in acting before graduation.
It explains why he decided to avoid theatre productions.
It illustrates how involvement with performers helped him find direction.
It proves that formal education was unnecessary for his career.
detail.why: Participating in theatre helped him find a sense of purpose and belonging.

detail.title: What does Ford's account of his uncertain early career challenge?
options: The assumption that a celebrated career necessarily began with quick success.
The idea that directors and writers contribute to successful films.
The belief that professional recognition can come later in life.
The possibility of having more than one occupation.
detail.why: His extended period of difficulty counters the impression that famous actors succeeded instantly.

detail.title: What responsibility does he connect with professional success?
options: To avoid accepting help from more experienced colleagues.
To continue playing the same roles that made one famous.
To choose only projects that guarantee financial success.
To create opportunities and support others in the profession.
detail.why: He presents the freedom gained through success as a reason to lift others up.

sequence: He remembers how discovering a place among performers gave him direction.
He reflects on the many contributors who make stories and films possible.
He turns his gratitude into an encouragement to support other people.

facts.title: Mention one kind of behind-the-scenes film professional whose contribution Ford values.
facts.answer: For example: a writer, director or member of the film crew.
facts.criteria: Accept one role explicitly named in the speech; an actor alone does not answer behind-the-scenes.

open.title: In two short sentences, explain how Ford's account connects personal success with other people's help.
open.answer: He describes finding direction through others and repeatedly acknowledges the people involved in his films. His success is shown as part of collective work rather than an individual achievement.
open.criteria: Credit one supported early influence and one example of collaboration or gratitude. Meaning-based review required.
